explanation: For each pair of prefixes, choose the cheapest insertion, deletion or substitution. Equal final characters require no edit. Only the previous row and current row are needed.
timeComplexity: O(mn). There are at most (m+1)(n+1) prefix pairs with three predecessor choices; iterative code keeps two short rows.
spaceComplexity: O(min(m,n)). Iterative variants keep two rows over the shorter string; memoized variants retain prefix-pair states and recursive frames.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Each table entry is the minimum cost for its two prefixes. Removing an optimal edit sequence’s final operation leaves one of the insertion, deletion or substitution predecessor prefixes; taking their minimum is therefore both attainable and necessary. Equal final characters can share the optimal shorter-prefix result without an edit.
walkthrough: To turn "cat" into "cut", keep c, substitute a with u, and keep t. The prefix recurrence charges exactly one substitution, so the result is 1. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: An empty string requires inserting or deleting every character of the other string.
Substitution costs one, rather than a deletion plus insertion.
